title: Imports and Dependencies
content: Imports Mathlib's prime number basics, finite set infrastructure, natural number foundations, and tactic framework. `Nat.Prime` provides the primality predicate and `Set.Infinite`/`Set.Finite` enable stating the infinitude conjectures.
mathContext: Uses `Nat.Prime p` ($p$ is prime), `Set.Infinite S` ($|S| = \infty$), and decision procedures (`decide`, `norm_num`) for computational verification.

title: Problem Statement and Historical Context
content: Module docstring describing Erdős Problem #1065 (Guy's B46): are there infinitely many primes $p$ with $p - 1 = 2^k q$ ($q$ prime)? Lists known examples, connections to safe primes and Artin's conjecture, and the more general $2^k 3^l q + 1$ variant. References OEIS A074781 (safe primes) and A339465.
mathContext: The problem asks about the density of primes whose predecessor $p-1$ has restricted factorization. Connected to Hardy-Littlewood Conjecture F (1923) on the density of safe primes: $\pi_{\text{safe}}(x) \sim 2C_2 x/(\log x)^2$.

title: Primes of the Form $2^k \cdot q + 1$
content:
Defines the predicate `IsTwoTimePrimePlusOne p`: a prime $p$ such that $p - 1 = 2^k \cdot q$ for some prime $q$ and non-negative integer $k$. This restricts $p - 1$ to have exactly one odd prime factor. The condition means $p - 1$ is '$2$-smooth times a prime', or equivalently that $p - 1$ has at most two distinct prime factors (2 and $q$).

The $k = 1$ case ($p = 2q + 1$) gives the safe primes (see `sophie-germain`), critical in Diffie-Hellman cryptography where $p - 1$ must resist Pohlig-Hellman factoring. The Euler totient $\varphi(p) = p - 1 = 2^k q$ (see `euler-totient`) has a restricted number of divisors, making the discrete logarithm problem in $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}^*$ harder when $p$ is a Form A prime.
mathContext: $\text{IsTwoTimePrimePlusOne}(p) \;:\Leftrightarrow\; p \text{ prime} \wedge \exists q, k \in \mathbb{N}: q \text{ prime} \wedge p = 2^k q + 1$. When $k = 0$, $p = q + 1$, so $p = 3, q = 2$ is the only solution. When $k = 1$, $p = 2q + 1$: these are the safe primes. The constraint $\omega(p-1) \leq 2$ (at most 2 distinct prime factors) is equivalent to the definition.

title: Primes of the Form $2^k \cdot 3^l \cdot q + 1$
content: Defines the relaxed predicate `IsTwoThreeTimePrimePlusOne p`: a prime $p$ such that $p - 1 = 2^k \cdot 3^l \cdot q$ for some prime $q$ and $k, l \geq 0$. This allows $p - 1$ to have up to three distinct prime factors. Setting $l = 0$ recovers the stronger form, so every $2^k q + 1$ prime is automatically a $2^k 3^l q + 1$ prime.
mathContext: $\text{IsTwoThreeTimePrimePlusOne}(p) \;:\Leftrightarrow\; p \text{ prime} \wedge \exists q, k, l \in \mathbb{N}: q \text{ prime} \wedge p = 2^k \cdot 3^l \cdot q + 1$. The set of such primes contains the Form A primes as $\{l = 0\} \subseteq \{l \geq 0\}$.

title: Conjecture A: Infinitely Many $2^k q + 1$ Primes
content: The stronger variant of Erdős Problem #1065: the set $\{p \text{ prime} : p - 1 = 2^k q,\; q \text{ prime}\}$ is infinite. This implies the safe primes conjecture as a special case ($k = 1$). The conjecture relates to the distribution of prime values of the polynomial $2^k q + 1$ as $q$ ranges over primes and $k$ over non-negative integers.

title: Conjecture B: Infinitely Many $2^k 3^l q + 1$ Primes
content: The weaker variant of Problem #1065: the set of primes $p$ with $p - 1 = 2^k \cdot 3^l \cdot q$ ($q$ prime) is infinite. This is implied by Conjecture A (set $l = 0$). The extra factor of $3^l$ significantly enlarges the candidate set — for example, $p = 61$ satisfies Form B but not Form A.

title: Computationally Verified Examples
content: Proves specific instances of Form A primes: $3 = 2^0 \cdot 2 + 1$, $5 = 2^1 \cdot 2 + 1$, $7 = 2^1 \cdot 3 + 1$, $11 = 2^1 \cdot 5 + 1$, $13 = 2^2 \cdot 3 + 1$, $29 = 2^2 \cdot 7 + 1$, $41 = 2^3 \cdot 5 + 1$, $97 = 2^5 \cdot 3 + 1$. Also proves $61 = 2^2 \cdot 3^1 \cdot 5 + 1$ is Form B but not Form A (since $60 = 4 \cdot 15$ and 15 is not prime). All proofs use Lean's `decide` and `norm_num` decision procedures.
mathContext: Eight primes $\leq 100$ satisfy Form A. The decompositions are: $p - 1 = 2^k q$ where $(p, k, q)$ ranges over $(3,0,2), (5,1,2), (7,1,3), (11,1,5), (13,2,3), (29,2,7), (41,3,5), (97,5,3)$.

title: Non-Example: $p = 37$
content: The prime $p = 37$ satisfies neither Form A nor Form B. We have $36 = 2^2 \cdot 3^2$, so $p - 1$ is a perfect $\{2,3\}$-smooth number with no additional prime factor $q$. This shows that not all primes satisfy even the relaxed form — the conditions are genuinely restrictive.
mathContext: $37 - 1 = 36 = 2^2 \cdot 3^2$. No factorization $2^k \cdot q$ or $2^k \cdot 3^l \cdot q$ yields $q$ prime, since $36/2^k$ for $k=0,1,2$ gives $36, 18, 9$ (all composite) and $36/(2^k 3^l)$ for valid $k,l$ gives only $1$ (not prime).

title: Form A Implies Form B
content: Proves that every prime of the $2^k q + 1$ form is also of the $2^k 3^l q + 1$ form, by taking $l = 0$ (so $3^0 = 1$). The proof destructures the Form A hypothesis and applies the trivial embedding. This establishes a set inclusion $\{\text{Form A primes}\} \subseteq \{\text{Form B primes}\}$.

title: Connection to Sophie Germain / Safe Primes
content:
Proves that the infinitude of safe primes ($p = 2q + 1$ with $q$ prime, see `sophie-germain`) would imply Conjecture A. A safe prime $p = 2q + 1$ is exactly a Form A prime with $k = 1$. The safe primes conjecture is itself wide open — heuristically, Hardy-Littlewood Conjecture F predicts $\sim 2C_2 \cdot x / (\log x)^2$ safe primes up to $x$ where $C_2 \approx 0.66$ is the twin primes constant.

The connection to Dirichlet's theorem (see `dirichlets-theorem`) is instructive: Dirichlet proved infinitely many primes in $a + nd$ (arithmetic progressions), while this conjecture asks about primes in $2^k q + 1$ where $q$ varies over primes — a much more restrictive structured set requiring two simultaneous primality conditions ($p$ and $q$ both prime).
mathContext: $\{p \in \mathbb{P} : \exists q \in \mathbb{P},\, p = 2q+1\} \subseteq \{p : \text{IsTwoTimePrimePlusOne}(p)\}$ via $k = 1$. Hardy–Littlewood predict $\pi_{\text{safe}}(x) \sim 2C_2 x/(\ln x)^2$.

title: Smooth Structure of $p - 1$
content: Extracts the factorization $p - 1 = 2^k \cdot q$ from the Form A hypothesis. The significance is that $p - 1$ is '$2$-smooth times a prime': its largest prime factor is $q$ and all other factors are powers of 2. This connects to the classical study of the factorization of $p - 1$ initiated by Artin's conjecture on primitive roots.
mathContext: $\text{IsTwoTimePrimePlusOne}(p) \implies p - 1 = 2^k q$ with $q$ prime. The number $p - 1$ is $q$-smooth with $\omega(p-1) \leq 2$.

title: Conjecture A Implies Conjecture B
content: Proves that if the set of Form A primes is infinite, then the set of Form B primes is infinite. Uses `Set.Infinite.mono` with `form_a_implies_b` to lift the set inclusion to an infinitude implication. This formalizes the logical hierarchy: safe primes $\Rightarrow$ Conjecture A $\Rightarrow$ Conjecture B.

title: Decidable Check Function
content: Implements a bounded decidable check `checkTwoTimePrime p` that tests whether $p$ is of the $2^k q + 1$ form by iterating over all $k < p$ and checking if $(p-1)/2^k$ is prime. This is a brute-force algorithm but suffices for small examples. The function returns `Bool` rather than `Prop`, enabling `#eval` computation.
mathContext: Algorithm: for each $k = 0, 1, \ldots, p-1$, check if $2^k \mid (p-1)$ and $(p-1)/2^k$ is prime. Complexity: $O(p \cdot T_{\text{prime}}(p))$ where $T_{\text{prime}}$ is the cost of primality testing.

title: Collective Verification of Eight Examples
content: Proves that all eight identified primes $\leq 100$ satisfy `IsTwoTimePrimePlusOne`, packaging the individual examples into a single universally quantified statement over a list. Uses `List.mem_cons` and case splitting to dispatch each element to its previously proved instance.
mathContext: $\forall p \in \{3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 29, 41, 97\}: \text{IsTwoTimePrimePlusOne}(p)$. These are all Form A primes $\leq 100$; note 17, 19, 23, 31, 37, 43, 47, 53, 59, 61, 67, 71, 73, 79, 83, 89 are excluded.
